rules.text_says: Condition Overload adds melee damage per status type; Furious Javelin adds melee damage.
rules.reported: Against overguard with no crits, Exalted Blade's light-attack parts split apart. With Condition Overload the direct hit gains less than an equal amount of raw melee damage, but the wave gains far more: one status lifted the wave about 245% where the equivalent Pressure Point gain did not. Furious Javelin stayed a clean x1.15 on hit and wave with no Condition Overload, and that x1.15 did not hold on light waves once Condition Overload was in.
rules.build_impact: For a blade used for waves, take Condition Overload and Furious Javelin together even at low Strength. If you mostly land direct hits, raw melee damage is better. Heavy waves stay the fully multiplicative case.
rules.creator_caveat: The creator could not fit a formula to the light wave numbers and asked viewers to help; the raw data is in the video description.

wiki.detail: Notes say the bonus does not multiply with Condition Overload where that interaction is additive, and the mechanic page treats Furious Javelin as a special case. No figure for light waves is listed.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.reported: Elemental mods and melee damage mods feed Furious Javelin the same way on Exalted Blade. Going from 60% to 165% on either or both always left its bonus at exactly the same 15%, so its value does not depend on how you reached your damage.
rules.build_impact: Choose between elemental and raw damage mods for other reasons, such as the status table or Condition Overload; Furious Javelin does not favor one.

wiki.detail: States the multiplicative melee bonus, and does not address elemental mods in particular.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.reported: Exalted Blade's light-attack wave sometimes does about a third of its normal damage, repeatably, with or without Furious Javelin or Condition Overload. This was seen in the Simulacrum, and the creator suspects real missions too.
rules.build_impact: Don't judge a blade build from a single wave number. Compare several hits before crediting or blaming a mod.
rules.creator_caveat: Bug seen in the Simulacrum only; the creator hopes it isn't in real missions but expects it is.

wiki.detail: Page lists 40% per second falloff and 20% loss per enemy hit, and no one-third bug.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.reported: Condition Overload did not scale Slash Dash's own damage in the creator's older test. It can still pay off because each Slash Dash hit throws waves: a wave hitting the enemy behind your target applies status first, and then Slash Dash stacks with those procs for Melee Afflictions and Healing Return.
rules.build_impact: On an Excalibur built around Slash Dash, value Condition Overload for the waves it powers, and use waves as primers for the dash.
rules.creator_caveat: The Slash Dash check is from an older test and he plans to retest it.

wiki.detail: Confirms Slash Dash uses Exalted Blade's mods and releases a wave per hit; says nothing on Condition Overload scaling of the dash.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.reported: Condition Overload also applies to finishers. Priming the target before the finisher does much more damage than the same finisher on a clean target. Separately, the bonus outlasts the status: after procs of about 6 seconds, the target keeps counting as primed for around 10 to 15 seconds.
rules.build_impact: On finisher builds such as Ultimatum or Radiant Finish, prime first. When testing damage, wait well past status duration before measuring a 'no status' baseline, or the numbers are contaminated.
rules.creator_caveat: Timing is the creator's rough estimate.

wiki.detail: Page lists stance and weapon multipliers, with no statement on the lingering window.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.reported: An Exalted Blade build that drops crit mods entirely did more damage for the creator: Condition Overload plus four 60/60 elemental mods, a blast, radiation and magnetic spread, and Toxin from the emissive color. The 60/60 mods also keep the status table even: swapping one for a 90% mod raised blast's share to almost twice toxin's, which costs distinct statuses for Condition Overload and Healing Return.
rules.build_impact: For a status-count blade build, prefer several smaller elemental mods over one big mod. Crit stops being a priority because base 15% plus Puncture's up to 25% flat crit still crits often. Radial Javelin does not get that Puncture bonus.
rules.creator_caveat: He says the Blast setup is still being tuned, and that it is meant for players using the blade almost exclusively.

wiki.detail: Confirms 15% base crit and status. The status weighting follows the general damage share rule on the Status Effect page.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Deep diving into Furious Javelin scaling, elemental vs melee damage and Condition Overload.

rules.text_says: Spliced Gas shows as ordinary elemental damage.
rules.reported: A Riven's spliced Gas damage is worth much more than its percentage suggests. Gas stat bonuses multiply each Gas proc tick as their own bucket, while Heat and Toxin mods that combine to make Gas don't touch it. So a lower Gas number can out-damage a much larger Heat plus Toxin total. Blast has no such bucket, which is the creator's reason to splice Gas ahead of it.
rules.build_impact: Splice Gas on Riven with toxin and heat stats, and compare it by tick damage, not by the modded damage readout. Range and Gas are the priority rolls on melee Influence builds; electricity can be replaced by a normal mod.

wiki.detail: The formula has a separate Gas Damage Bonuses term and says Heat and Toxin mods have no effect on tick damage.

source.creator: Agall
source.title: Splicing rivens for Gas, why its so powerful and weapon recommendations, demo of 4 examples

rules.reported: Heat is a better second element beside a Gas Riven than more Gas. Gas caps at 10 instances per target, while Heat keeps stacking. On an 80% base status weapon, Hammer Shot's status beats its crit damage value, and Galvanized Aptitude may not be worth a slot when it is not multiplicative on that weapon.
rules.build_impact: Once a Riven gives Gas, add Heat from a mod and put Hammer Shot before Galvanized Aptitude on high base status weapons.
rules.creator_caveat: The creator's judgment of Galvanized Aptitude is hedged, resting on what he has read about that weapon.

wiki.detail: Confirms a 10-instance limit on Gas.

source.title: Splicing rivens for Gas, why its so powerful and weapon recommendations, demo of 4 examples

rules.reported: Tenet Tetra's alt-fire grenade consumes the magazine and its damage scales with how full the magazine is as a share, not with its size. Magazine mods don't make the grenade stronger; they only spread the same full damage over more bullets.
rules.build_impact: Don't use magazine mods to raise grenade damage. Fire it from a full magazine, and leave capacity out unless you want the rounds for normal fire.

wiki.detail: Says damage scales linearly with percentage of remaining magazine and not with capacity modding.

source.creator: QuadLyStop
source.title: 56 Warframe Gun Mechanics Every Player Should Know

rules.reported: Elements on a weapon combine in a set priority: modded elements first, then the weapon's innate element, then outside sources such as Violet Archon Shards, in that order. Innate elements also don't count as a built-in elemental mod: a 90% mod adds its full 90% on top of them.
rules.build_impact: When a shard or innate element is meant to create a combination, check it won't get pulled into or out of a combination by a mod placed earlier in the order.

wiki.detail: Describes the top-left-first mod hierarchy with innate elements considered last. Shards are not covered in that passage.

rules.reported: On Banshee, Primary Debilitate's extra Heat, Electricity and Toxin procs redip the Sonar multiplier. On Phantasma, with innate radiation plus magnetic and corrosive, its combined statuses split into base-element damage over time that doubles up on Sonar's weak point bonus and reaches very high numbers.
rules.build_impact: Stack combined elements for Debilitate instead of pure Heat when running Sonar on a chain or beam status primary.

wiki.detail: Notes that extra statuses are separate instances that multiply DoTs. The Sonar page confirms DoTs are calculated from the boosted hit, and that area DoTs double dip.

source.creator: KeesieOilcorner
source.title: Banshee Is A MUST USE In Void Cascade - [Warframe]

rules.reported: Evade should go up right after another cast. Arcane Concentration doesn't apply to the cast that triggers it, so casting a cheap ability like Sonic Boom first means Evade starts with that +60% Duration, and with enough weak point kills that longer maximum holds for the whole mission.
rules.build_impact: For any long-held subsumed buff on a Duration build, cast a cheap ability before it.

wiki.detail: Notes say the effect does not apply to the ability that granted the buff.

source.creator: KeesieOilcorner
source.title: Banshee Is A MUST USE In Void Cascade - [Warframe]

rules.reported: Anabolic Pollination gives a separate Toxin damage buff that does not combine with your weapons' elements, and it also works on Dual Ichor. That gives a Toxin source without disturbing the weapon's status table setup.
rules.build_impact: A Pharaoh Predasite is a cheap Toxin source on builds that need the element kept apart, such as Dual Ichor; the creator pairs it with Banshee in Void Cascade.

wiki.detail: Says the Toxin bonus does not combine with other elements and affects all players' weapons.

source.title: Banshee Is A MUST USE In Void Cascade - [Warframe]

rules.reported: Subsumed Evade on Nova can stay up passively because Molecular Prime explosions and Okina hits land headshots, and Gas procs from a Gas and Influence Okina headshot too. That permanent invisibility keeps Arcane Crepuscular active with almost no input, in a build meant to run as a low-effort farm.
rules.build_impact: Core parts: Nova, Evade, Arcane Crepuscular, Equilibrium, a Gas plus Influence Okina with Condition Overload, and a Nautilus or Verglas companion. Hot Shot and Equilibrium cover the rest. The creator notes it may not last, as it is a highly passive farm.
rules.creator_caveat: Brozime credits another creator for the discovery; he thinks such passive setups may be removed later.

wiki.detail: Lists Molecular Prime headshot kills stacking Deadhead arcanes, so explosions can register headshots. The Evade page confirms weak point kills extend it.

source.creator: Brozime
source.title: Nova Prime Breaks Bad the Weird Way | Warframe Recursive Build

rules.reported: Up to four Molecular Prime waves can run at once. Recasting every quarter of the wave's duration keeps a maximum-range wave out at all times; the creator finds recasting around halfway good enough.
rules.build_impact: Because wave size follows Duration, a Duration-stacked Nova can recast about every 5 seconds and hold the map primed without maxing Range.

wiki.detail: Tips say recasting gives wider average coverage as the first wave collapses. The limit of four isn't stated.

rules.reported: Heads usually have one Sonar node but other body parts have two, and nodes multiply each other. At 200% Strength a two-node leg gives 10 x 10 = 100x, while a critical head with one node is 10 x 6 = 60x. So above a low Strength, you should shoot highlighted bodies and not aim for the head. Tripling Strength also squares the payoff: 5x becomes 15x, but 25x becomes 225x.
rules.build_impact: Sonar Strength is worth far more than the sheet suggests, because two-node parts square it. Spam Sonar until a part has two highlights; target the highlighted limb, not the highlighted shape, since only the actual hitbox counts.

wiki.detail: Says most parts have 2 nodes and heads usually 1, nodes multiply, and critical hits on Sonar spots don't become headcrits. Natural head multipliers apply only to heads.

rules.reported: Blast procs can use Sonar twice. The hit's multiplier sets the proc's value, and the detonation can hit a weak point and get it again: 225 x 225 gives about 50,625x in a 15x two-node setup. It gets high enough to break the weapon: on Sabaris's Incarnon form, its area effect appeared to stop working once damage reached quintillions.
rules.build_impact: On Banshee, a weapon with forced Blast or innate Blast gains much more than its crit sheet suggests. Past the damage cap, more is wasted or can hurt the area effect.
rules.creator_caveat: The Sabaris failure was an observation, not a deliberate test.

wiki.detail: Says 10-stack and on-death Blast can double dip the Sonar effect. The Sabaris behavior isn't mentioned.

rules.reported: Some non-humanoid enemies have many nodes on one body part, such as Techrot Babau's chest. Sonar keeps multiplying on them, enough that a Lex with only Pistol Gambit did over 15 million damage on one in the test.
rules.build_impact: Against these enemies, spam Sonar before shooting. A cheap weapon is enough.

wiki.detail: Names Techrot Babau and The Anatomizer as having far more than 2 nodes, stacking for extremely high multipliers.

rules.reported: Since Sonar spots count as weak points, any body-shot kill on a highlight refreshes subsumed Evade. Evade's weak point healing can trigger Archon Intensify too, as long as you need healing. Combat Discipline's self-damage on kills supplies that need even while invisible, keeping up +30% from Intensify and +30% from Crepuscular, taking a 130% build to about 190% Strength in mission.
rules.build_impact: Count that conditional Strength when planning Sonar's reach. Combat Discipline also triggers Arcane Avenger through its self-damage, though the creator calls that extra overkill.

wiki.detail: Says Sonar spots count as Weak Points for effects. The Evade page confirms duration and health on weak point kills. Combat Discipline confirms self damage.

rules.reported: Crux-type arcanes trigger from Sonar's weak points. A spliced Riven with about 40% or more Ammo Efficiency plus Crux's 60% reaches 100% with no headshots needed, giving unlimited ammo on any weapon, including a one-round magazine.
rules.build_impact: Old: worth doing on low-magazine, high-damage weapons on Banshee. Now: a Crux needs only about 15% more to reach the 75% cap, so don't spend a Riven slot beyond that. The Sonar trigger for Crux still works.

wiki.detail: Confirms weak point triggering for mods and arcanes; the Riven page lists the spliced Ammo Efficiency attribute.

later_patch.detail: Ammo Efficiency is now capped at 75% across all sources, so this Riven and Crux stack no longer gives 100%. Infinite ammo now comes only from specific effects such as Arcane Pistoleer.

rules.reported: Silence removes Eximus auras too, so a Guardian Eximus can't give nearby enemies its 90% damage reduction, which works out to about 10x damage against them. Acolytes can't cast either, with one exception: Misery's summons of shadow Acolytes appear to ignore it.
rules.build_impact: Keep Silence up in rooms with protective Eximus and for Acolytes. Don't count on it against Misery's summons.

wiki.detail: Confirms enemies can't activate abilities. It doesn't discuss Eximus auras or Misery.

rules.reported: Gaseous Quake's damage multiplier grows each second of channeling while energy cost also rises, and the cost has no cap, so it can't run forever even with team energy support. Solo the creator reaches around 10 to 15 seconds with Brightbonnet, and around 30 in a team.
rules.build_impact: Plan it as a timed burst, not a held ultimate. The maximum damage needs about 10 seconds, so total energy of about 614 before efficiency is the real entry requirement.

wiki.detail: Damage caps at 24,736x after 10 s of channeling. Drain multiplies 1.2x per second with no cap, costing about 614 energy.

rules.reported: Secondary Cryogenic's Cold is applied as a real weapon hit doing almost no damage. So it triggers on-hit effects on everything it reaches: Spectral Spirit's Doom chance, Citrine's Prismatic Gem beams on every enemy in range (a beam restarts on its next target about every 0.5 s), and Garuda's Seeking Talons Slash. The creator's frame is to find an on-hit effect that does the real damage for you.
rules.build_impact: A Puncture-capable pistol with Cryogenic can spread Gem beams to a whole group from one target, and it primes fast. Doom and Talons versions are curiosities that deal almost nothing themselves.

wiki.detail: Confirms Cold spreads around the target and uses weapon Status Duration. It does not discuss on-hit effects. Prismatic Gem's page lists a 0.4 s retarget delay against the creator's 0.5 s.

rules.reported: Punch through from universal weapon bonuses such as Corvex's passive also reaches ability projectiles coded like weapons. Tesla Nervos balls pass through the enemy and release after, instead of stopping on it. Another thrown pull ability from the same test went through the ground and failed to pull anyone.
rules.build_impact: Punch through makes these throws less reliable. The creator only found this useful as a curiosity and couldn't make damage from it.
rules.creator_caveat: The creator presents it as useless for damage.

wiki.detail: The page makes no mention of punch through.

rules.reported: Blast procs from Melee Afflictions used to do 1 damage each when no other damaging status was on the target, and they now do their full value, with no announcement. With innate Blast and 100% slam status, a Jat Kittag slam stacks and detonates enough blast for Afflictions to deal real damage, and Vulcan Blitz spreads its explosions through Saryn in the same way as Acid Shells did on the Sobek.
rules.build_impact: Blast Afflictions on heavy melee became usable in June. Treat the Vulcan Blitz half as old; its explosion rules were reworked in the same 44.1.3 change as Acid Shells.

later_patch.detail: Vulcan Blitz is listed with Explosive Demise, Combustion Beam, Thermagnetic Shells and Entropy Detonation in the Acid Shells nerf.

wiki.detail: Notes say Blast instances from Afflictions now deal intended damage with no other damaging status, flagged as unconfirmed on which patch.

source.title: Incredible ways to deal one damage

rules.reported: Jat Kittag's slam has 100% base status instead of the normal 25%. Weeping Wounds multiplies base status, so on a slam one combo stage gives 40% more base value, and at 5x combo it adds 200% status with no other status mods.
rules.build_impact: Status-chance mods are close to unnecessary for its slams. A Blast slam Afflictions build frees slots, and Influence is another choice that stacks fast.

wiki.detail: Lists slam attacks with 100% status chance and innate Blast. Weeping Wounds lists 40% per combo tier on base status.

rules.reported: Amalgam Furax Body Count's melee-kill Blast procs do 1 damage each, but Melee Influence spreads them. A melee kill among 20 enemies produces about five Blast procs on each, with another copy from Influence, and these procs mask the Electricity damage that is actually killing them. It is a way to generate many stacks, not damage by itself.
rules.build_impact: Good for a mod already used as a +45% fire rate stat stick. Don't count its blast as damage, but its stacks do feed Melee Influence setups.

wiki.detail: States about 6 Blast procs at 1 damage per stack. Influence spreading isn't covered.

source.creator: IgnusT
source.title: Incredible ways to deal one damage

later_patch.detail: Listed among the explode-on-death mods whose death effect can no longer be retriggered by status from Elemental Ammo. Spreading its procs with Melee Influence is not named in that note.

rules.reported: Primary Compression only shrinks the Proboscis Cernos's final blast; the tendril pull stays the same range and its hits take the damage bonus. So the arcane keeps an area-of-effect function on this weapon, unlike the usual cost of becoming single target.
rules.build_impact: One of the few explosive weapons that loses little with Compression. It suits a build leaning on tendril hits, though the creator says those aren't most of the weapon's damage.

wiki.detail: Says Firestorm and Primary Compression only affect the final blast radius and not tendril range.

rules.reported: Shadow is treated as an extension of Sevagoth for conditions. Damage taken as Shadow can trigger Sevagoth's on-damaged arcanes such as Aegis and Avenger, and Shadow's rolls can trigger on-roll arcanes. Shadow also activates Health and Energy Conversion, and a Claw headshot triggers Leaded Gas on your main weapon.
rules.build_impact: Sevagoth's main loadout arcanes can be fed from Shadow form, so you can choose them for Shadow's gameplay without losing them as Sevagoth.
rules.creator_caveat: From 24 hours of solo testing. He admits he may have missed cases.

wiki.detail: Lists Shadow Claws as working for unattributed effects in Sevagoth's arsenal; these on-damage conditions aren't individually listed.

source.title: Warframe | Totally my Last Time Talking about Sevagoth

rules.reported: Reaching 12x on Shadow Claws with a combo mod lets you carry the combo-mod bonuses to Sevagoth's melee. Leaving Shadow form keeps those bonuses when the combo counter disappears. A heavy attack clears them unless done with Tennokai; building then losing combo inside Shadow resets the bonus to 1x.
rules.build_impact: Stack Blood Rush and Weeping Wounds on Shadow, then switch for one giant boosted window on the normal melee. Use Tennokai heavies to keep it.

wiki.detail: No matching note found.

rules.reported: Primary Debilitate on Shadow's Claws creates procs counted as pure damage from the weapon holding the arcane. They do not count as melee or ability damage, so they don't stack Arcane Impetus or Hot Shot. They do trigger that weapon's own on-death or low-health effects, including Acid Shells, as long as the Debilitate proc itself does the kill or brings the enemy low. Debilitate on an Arch-gun also works here.
rules.build_impact: Shadow can turn Debilitate into a remote trigger for main-loadout weapon effects, and on-death items on that weapon fire from Shadow's hits, which gives a melee-only form use of primary or Arch-gun passives.

later_patch.detail: Status effects from elemental ammo no longer retrigger death explosions for Acid Shells and the related mods. The video was uploaded before this patch.

rules.creator_caveat: Noted as hard to separate from other sources in his tests.

wiki.detail: Says Primary Debilitate's extra procs count as Primary Damage, and bonus instances attribute to the source class of the equipment.

A Debilitate only triggers from projectile abilities in Shade form through that route. Influence's damage also takes both the lingering source as a new base and Claw mods as a multiplier, so 100 from a primary with +100% Pressure Point on Claws gets multiplied further.
rules.build_impact: For Sevagoth with a projectile ability such as Tempest Barrage, mod Electricity on the source, and put Melee Influence on the Claws for proc spread and damage from both loadouts. Heat from Inherit makes this weaker.
rules.creator_caveat: He disagrees with part of the wiki and calls it his own testing result, inviting others to retest.

Harmony's heavy attack hits, makes a proc, and condenses it, so a Prime Smite plus Riven faction stat multiplies several times, which the creator calls a triple dip. Keep one Riven per faction, with a matching Smite mod, and don't mix factions. Where no Smite mod exists, as with Scaldra and Techrot, use Lasting Sting with a Riven faction stat. rules.reported: Arcane Sculptor locks Ability Efficiency at the 175% cap, which also cancels Blind Rage's cost penalty, but the cast that creates the object doesn't benefit. So a frame whose object ability is low priority risks an energy drought if the lock lapses. A subsumed Tesla Nervos is a cheap, unrestricted way to trigger it on any frame and also triggers Archon Stretch; Brightbonnet costs less than Dispensary and adds Strength.
rules.build_impact: Sculptor's best on frames whose main ability creates an object. Others should subsume Tesla Nervos or Brightbonnet, and hold energy for that first cast. Molt and Wil-O-Wisp are free of this delay.

wiki.detail: Notes confirm no benefit to the first proc ability and list valid objects including Brightbonnet and Tesla Nervos. Molt and Wil-O-Wisp spawn instantly, so their first cast does benefit.

rules.reported: Secondary Cryogenic needs a Puncture proc, and most primer secondaries such as Cycron, Pox and Kompressa don't have Puncture. Valence bonuses don't solve it, so it's a poor fit for its obvious use as a Cold primer; Epitaph has forced Cold in a larger radius.
rules.build_impact: Don't plan a primer around Cryogenic unless the weapon already has Puncture. For a damage secondary, arcane slots usually do more elsewhere.

Those shards make the electric version better against very high single targets, such as level 10,000 in Void Cascade.

rules.reported: Xata's Whisper's extra hit has a hidden -50% crit chance, so it normally can't crit. Headshot crit from Harrow's Covenant and from Ivara's reworked Concentrated Arrow are added late enough to escape that, and they stack: 200% from Covenant plus 75% from the Arrow, minus 50%, gives 225% and red crits. Arcane Avenger won't help here, and neither of these works on body shots. One Xata hit reached 7.2 million from an 83,000 arrow, and at level cap it reached the 2.1 billion cap.
rules.build_impact: Core parts: Ivara with Xata's Whisper subsumed, Artemis Bow with Concentrated Arrow, Primary Compression, Primed Firestorm, Primary Acuity, and Arcane Crepuscular plus Tenacious Bond to raise crit damage. Everything pays for high crit on one headshot, so it's for low-kill-rate missions such as Disruption. Mod some elemental damage too, because it raises the extra hit.
rules.creator_caveat: The -50% order-of-operations story is the creator's theory about the code, and he says he can't fully verify it. He needed an Extinguished Dragon Key to cut his damage enough to see the hits at all.

wiki.detail: Notes say it can crit with Covenant on headshots and with Concentrated Arrow on a fully charged headshot. The Concentrated Arrow page lists +50% on weak points where the video says 75%.

rules.reported: Primary Compression's 0.2x radius applies after mods, so blast radius mods raise its damage: every meter lost is +100%. To match a 360% arcane like Merciless or Deadhead, a weapon needs at least 4.5 m of radius. On Concentrated Arrow, Range and Firestorm add together and feed this, but Overextended loses damage overall in Xata setups because its Strength cost hurts Xata, Prowl's headshot multiplier and the bow.
rules.build_impact: Under about 4.5 m of radius, use a different arcane. On explosive weapons, Firestorm becomes a real damage mod. On Ivara, take Range from Stretch and Augur Reach rather than Overextended.

wiki.detail: Confirms 80% radius reduction on aim and +100% damage per meter lost, scaling smoothly, multiplicative on projectile weapons.

rules.reported: During a level cap run, the creator saw Primary Compression's buff stack up to about 9,000% extra damage and couldn't explain how. He planned to reverse engineer it from stream footage.
rules.build_impact: Don't plan on this; treat it as an unconfirmed bug.
rules.creator_caveat: Observed once, cause unknown.

wiki.detail: Stacking isn't described. The buff is normally derived from radius lost, so 9,000% would need 90 m lost.

rules.reported: On a multishot beam weapon, Ballistic Battery's stored damage and Ballistic Bullseye's flat crit are multiplied by multishot, because beams turn multishot into one larger damage instance. At 200% Bullseye and 20 multishot on Phantasma Prime that means 4,000% crit, around tier 40, and crit damage grows with the tier. Battery's stored damage is added after base damage mods, yet still takes elemental, faction, crit, headshot and status multipliers.
rules.build_impact: Core parts: Mesa with Battery and Bullseye, Phantasma Prime with Galvanized Hell and Primary Blight, toxin and blast, plus Roar or Shooting Gallery. A high-Strength Bullseye and any multishot beam is the main combination, and it lets you replace Regulators with something else.
rules.creator_caveat: The creator says Blast status shouldn't be able to crit and can't fully explain the damage cap Blast numbers.

wiki.detail: States the crit bonus is multiplied by multishot on beams without a radial component, naming Ocucor, Nukor and Enkaus. Ballistic Battery confirms the base damage rules, and only one projectile takes stored damage on non-beam multishot.

rules.reported: On Vauban, subsumed Jade Stars isn't for damage but a trigger for Hot Shot. Tesla Nervos hits and Bastille's per-second vortex tick both apply its Heat, and Hot Shot's 300% crit then works on Vauban's Tether Flechette Orb and his weapons. All of his abilities except the new Photon Strike create objects, so Sculptor stays at 175% efficiency almost all the time.
rules.build_impact: Core parts: Vauban, Jade Stars, Hot Shot, Sculptor, Worthy Comradery, plus an invisibility companion like Urus Kubrow or Shade Prime instead of a tank build. Bastille's armor gain of up to 1,500 also triggers Arcane Persistence and Primary Bulwark.

wiki.detail: Confirms crit chance when abilities inflict Heat. Sculptor's page lists Tesla Nervos as a valid object; Update 44 notes do not change this.

rules.reported: Vauban's Factor Overdrive Pad is a universal final multiplier, so it applies to every weapon and to abilities coded as weapons, including his Tether Flechette Orb. Vigorous Swap also works on the orb and multiplies with it: 2.65x times 1.73x. The orb's Puncture damage scales with enemy level, which is why it stays useful late.
rules.build_impact: Vigorous Swap suits Vauban's main damage ability, and his pad is a real squad buff worth placing where allies stand. The orb's level scaling means Strength and Sculptor efficiency are worth more than Range.

wiki.detail: Confirms a 25% weapon damage bonus on the Vector-Overdrive Pad, and that nail Puncture damage multiplies by ceil(enemy level / 10). The universal-final-multiplier wording isn't spelled out.

rules.reported: Trait locking and splicing change Riven math: a spliced stat is locked free, and locking any stat also fixes the plus and minus shape. Splicing can combine a positive and negative stat into one positive. A plan-first roll of shape, then one stat, then another stat takes about 20 rolls on average, against 310 when random, and about 108 rolls of Kuva instead of 2,208 for a full target. Keep a negative too: not having one skips power for no gain.
rules.build_impact: Roll for shape first and lock as you go, and stop at the right stat instead of chasing roll quality: the +/-10% variance is worth only about 1 to 3% real change except at a breakpoint. Spliced stats count, so plan the pair you need at the start.

later_patch.detail: Riven disposition was removed, so the part of the math about weapon disposition being fixed no longer varies by weapon as he describes. Spliced ammo efficiency also fell under the new 75% cap.

wiki.detail: The Trait Locking section confirms doubled Kuva on a locked trait. Update 44 notes confirm a spliced stat locks free and that a lock fixes positive and negative counts.
